failures.criterion: A client behind a TCP proxy that stops forwarding without closing either side reconnects within 60 s (shared code path). Reconnecting must not leave the hung redial's socket open.
failures.evidence: This change makes redials routine: every freeze now causes one, and a route that stays dead causes one every 22 s. When a redial is accepted and the server then sends nothing (row B's case), nats.js 2.29.3 stops waiting after its 20 s dial timeout but never closes the socket. protocol.js dial() calls transport.close(err), and node_transport.js _closed() returns at once because `if (!this.connected) return;`, so socket.destroy() never runs. Each such redial leaks one TCP socket for as long as the peer keeps it open. Red test: packages/envoy-client/src/__tests__/nats-stall.test.ts 'a redial that hangs is closed once nats.js gives up on it, so the client holds no socket to it' (commit a68f83db). Command: `cd packages/envoy-client && LEGION_E2E_ENVOY_STACK=1 bun test src/__tests__/nats-stall.test.ts -t "redial that hangs is closed"`. Result: (fail) [32194.66ms], expect(hung[0]?.closedAt).toBeDefined() got undefined, so the socket was still open 30 s after the accept. Then I edited node_modules/nats/lib/src/node_transport.js for one run only, so that _closed() destroys the socket when the connection is not connected: 1 pass, 'accepted 2.1 s after the drop, closed 20.0 s after it was accepted'. I restored node_modules after the run. The fix can be in envoy-client, such as a pinned patch of nats.js, or another choice of the implementer's. The test only asks that the abandoned socket is closed.

failures.criterion: The Claude Code plugin's code path recovers from a frozen path (consumer-visible: the MCP channel server Claude Code runs must still stop when Claude Code stops it)
failures.evidence: This is the effect of the leak above that a user can see. After one hung redial, the claude-envoy channel server never exits on SIGTERM. In my independent drive it was still running 120 s after SIGTERM (stderr was empty). Temporary stderr markers in shutdown() showed forwarder.close() and unregisterSession both finished, so the process stays alive only because of the leaked socket. Without a hung redial, it exits in 0.0 s (no freeze), 1.0 s (while frozen) and 0.0 s (after a recovery with no hung redial). Red test: packages/claude-envoy/tests/envoy-channel-stall.test.ts 'a session whose redial once hung still exits on SIGTERM' (commit 3b7ea79b). Command: `cd packages/claude-envoy && LEGION_E2E_ENVOY_STACK=1 bun test tests/envoy-channel-stall.test.ts -t "still exits on SIGTERM"`. Result: (fail) [65784.18ms], Expected "exited" Received "running" 15 s after SIGTERM. With the same one-run nats.js edit as above: 1 pass, 'SIGTERM -> exited after 0.0 s'.
